correctness.rationale: For L≥5 the periodic bipartite degree-three honeycomb H_L has no cycles of length <6 and its only six-cycles are cellular faces (any noncontractible cycle has length ≥2L). On radius-two graph cliques, a simplex of dimension ≥3 is one centered closed-neighborhood tetrahedron; unique midpoints follow from absence of 4-cycles. Every remaining maximal triangle is one of two alternating vertex triples per hexagon. Center tetrahedra collapse relative to H_L by tetrahedron/opposite triangle then each center triangle/opposite distance-two edge; the two exceptional 2-cell boundaries map to the same face hexagon. Attaching one per face gives the torus; the second nullhomotopic attachment wedges L² 2-spheres. The face-cycle boundary map has exactly one integral face relation, giving primitive kernel rank L²−1 and H1=Z², H2=Z^{L²+1}. Independently rebuilt H5 and H6 radius-two face taxonomy, confirming face vectors and 2L² noncentered triangles; finite checks do not replace the all-L cellulation argument.
